title: Platform: unified observability data erasure & scoped retention playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and implement a reproducible playbook for erasing/retaining observability data (traces, logs, metrics) that balances developer debugging needs with tenant privacy, cost, and regulatory constraints. Scope covers ingestion-time hygiene (tracing hooks, collector transforms), downstream pipeline controls (sampling, TTLs), storage enforcement (rolling retention, tombstones), tenant-scoped access controls, and an erasure API for compliance requests.

Problem summary: Current tracing and log pipelines occasionally capture user-identifying strings (email, phone, document IDs) in: span attributes, debug-level logs, and some structured fields emitted by SDKs. Retention rules are inconsistent across systems (Kafka -> long-term ClickHouse vs. ephemeral metrics DB), and query/UIs lack fine-grained RBAC and immutable access logs for who accessed PII-containing telemetry. We need a single operational playbook and an implementable migration plan.

Key design decisions proposed: 
- Instrumentation & tracing hooks: add a lightweight sanitizer in our SDKs (node/python/go) that applies configurable field allowlists + regex-based redaction at SDK-level for known user fields; emit an additional sanitized copy of spans to a separate "observability-sanitized" topic for long-term storage. For traces carrying customer-supplied context (customer_id, request_id), preserve only tenant-scoped identifiers and drop user identifiers.
- Ingestion transforms vs storage-time masking: perform deterministic pseudonymization (HMAC with tenant-scoped key) for identifiers that must remain linkable for debugging across systems. Keep raw-elision by default: raw PII should never be stored in long-term backends. For cases where raw detail is required, require explicit opt-in with a documented security review and KMS-protected envelope.
- Sampling & retention: introduce tenant-configurable retention profiles (e.g., debug=30d, standard=7d, restricted=3d) with default conservative retention. Sampling policy will be hierarchical: client-side rate limits -> collector sampling -> storage TTLs. Sampling metadata (why/when sample kept) must be stored as non-PII attributes.
- RBAC & access logging: extend the Console and the query gateway to support column-level ACLs on observability views (e.g., allowlist which teams can see certain span tags). All access to raw telemetry or any field flagged as sensitive must generate immutable access log entries stored in an audit system with 7-year retention for enterprise customers that require it.
- Erasure API: implement a tenant-scoped erasure endpoint that: (1) locates matching keys across all telemetry stores by pseudonymized identifier, (2) deletes or tombstones records beyond legal hold, and (3) writes an immutable audit record of the erasure operation. Erasure must be asynchronous with per-tenant progress tracking.

Trade-offs & risks: 
- Performance: SDK sanitization adds CPU cost on client side; ingestion transforms add latency (~5-15ms per event in worst case). We'll benchmark and gate default sanitization by sampling and runtime flags.
- Debugging vs privacy: pseudonymization preserves linkability for debugging but is irreversible without tenant keys; for on-call workflows we will provide time-bound ephemeral access workflows (just-in-time access with MFA and audit).
- Operator complexity: adding per-tenant retention profiles increases configuration surface. We'll provide sane defaults and a migration script for tenants on legacy profiles.

Implementation plan (phases): 
1) Phase 1 - Instrumentation & collector transforms (sprint 1-2): Ship SDK sanitizer with toggle; add ingestion transform in the collector to drop known PII fields and emit sanitized topic.
2) Phase 2 - Pseudonymization and TTL enforcement (sprint 3-4): Add HMAC-based pseudonymization module (tenant-keyed) in the pipeline, propagate pseudonym ID through downstream backends, enforce TTLs at storage layer with background compaction jobs.
3) Phase 3 - RBAC + audit (sprint 5-6): Add column-level ACL checks in query gateway and immutable access log writer; integrate with Console UI to surface access history.
4) Phase 4 - Erasure API + migration (sprint 7-8): Implement asynchronous erasure, migration tooling to reprocess historical telemetry and apply redaction/tombstones.

Rollout & migration: Start with opt-in for internal teams (dev + platform) and a single pilot customer. Provide a migration job to reprocess N days of historical telemetry into the sanitized topic; allow rollbacks. Provide runbooks for on-call (how to investigate errors when sanitization removes useful debug context).

Success metrics: percentage reduction in sampled traces containing PII (target >95% within pilot), latency increase at ingestion <10ms p50, successful erasure request completion time <24h for small datasets, adoption by 3 pilot tenants in Q2 2026.

Open questions: list of fields per language SDK to default-redact; KMS key rotation implications on pseudonymization; legal hold workflows for customers who require longer retention.
